words.explanation: 신문이나 뉴스에서 기사의 가장 위에 있는 큰 제목으로, 독자의 관심을 끌기 위해 만들어짐
words.example_from_convo: The headline read 'Breaking News: Major Policy Change Announced'
words.example_ko: 그 헤드라인은 '속보: 주요 정책 변화 발표됨'이라고 읽혀 있었다
words.tip: 동의어: title, heading / 반의어: body text / 출제영역: 뉴스, 미디어

words.explanation: 특정 지역이나 분야에서 뉴스를 수집하여 보도하는 기자 또는 통신사의 직원
words.example_from_convo: Our foreign correspondent reported live from the capital city
words.example_ko: 우리의 해외 특파원이 수도에서 실시간으로 보도했다
words.tip: 동의어: reporter, journalist / 반의어: editor / 출제영역: 언론, 직업

words.explanation: 뉴스 매체가 어떤 사건이나 주제에 대해 얼마나 광범위하게 보도하는지를 나타냄
words.example_from_convo: The election received extensive coverage from all major networks
words.example_ko: 그 선거는 모든 주요 방송국으로부터 광범위한 보도를 받았다
words.tip: 동의어: reporting, publicity / 반의어: obscurity / 출제영역: 미디어, 저널리즘

words.explanation: 업무나 책임을 다른 사람에게 맡기거나, 다른 사람을 대신하여 권력이나 의견을 표현하는 사람
words.example_from_convo: The manager decided to delegate the project to his team members
words.example_ko: 그 관리자는 그 프로젝트를 팀 멤버들에게 위임하기로 결정했다
words.tip: 동의어: assign, authorize / 반의어: retain, monopolize / 출제영역: 비즈니스, 직장

words.explanation: 여러 개의 것들을 하나로 합치거나, 어떤 상태나 위치를 더욱 견고하게 만드는 것
words.example_from_convo: The company decided to consolidate its regional offices into one headquarters
words.example_ko: 그 회사는 지역 지사들을 하나의 본사로 통합하기로 결정했다
words.tip: 동의어: combine, merge / 반의어: separate, divide / 출제영역: 비즈니스, 조직

quiz.question: In a news context, a headline is MOST similar to which of the following?
options: A detailed analysis of an event
The main title of a news article designed to grab attention
A personal opinion about a topic
The body text of a story
quiz.explanation: A headline is the prominent title at the top of a news article meant to capture readers' interest, similar to how a title summarizes content.
option_explanations: This describes an editorial or op-ed, not a headline
Correct - this is the definition of a headline
This is opinion writing, not a headline
This is the main content, not the headline

quiz.question: Which word best completes this sentence? 'A foreign ___ works in another country to report news back to their home network.'
options: editor
correspondent
publisher
commentator
quiz.explanation: A correspondent is a journalist who reports news from a specific location or region, typically working for a news organization.
option_explanations: An editor supervises writers but doesn't typically report from foreign locations
Correct - a correspondent reports news from specific regions
A publisher prints or distributes content
A commentator offers analysis and opinions

quiz.question: What does extensive news coverage of an event typically indicate?
options: The event was ignored by media
The event received detailed and widespread reporting from multiple sources
The event happened in a remote location
The event was not important enough for news
quiz.explanation: Extensive coverage means many media outlets reported on the event in detail and from various angles.
option_explanations: Opposite of extensive coverage
Correct - extensive coverage means widespread and detailed reporting
Coverage amount is independent of location
Extensive coverage shows importance

quiz.question: When a business consolidates its departments, what does it do?
options: It hires more employees
It closes all operations
It merges multiple departments into one unified structure
It moves to a different country
quiz.explanation: To consolidate means to combine separate entities or functions into one integrated whole to improve efficiency or strength.
option_explanations: Consolidation may reduce or redistribute staff, not necessarily hire
Consolidation improves the business; it doesn't close it
Correct - consolidation merges separate units into one
Consolidation is typically about internal restructuring

quiz.question: Which situation best demonstrates the meaning of 'to delegate'?
options: A manager completes all the work herself to ensure quality
A manager assigns specific tasks to team members and trusts them to complete the work
A manager criticizes her team for poor performance
A manager cancels a project entirely
quiz.explanation: Delegating means assigning responsibility or tasks to others, trusting them to handle the work.
option_explanations: This is the opposite of delegating
Correct - delegating involves assigning tasks to others
This is criticism, not delegation
This is cancellation, not delegation

quiz.sentence: The newspaper's front-page ___ announced the discovery of a new renewable energy source that could revolutionize the industry.
quiz.sentence_ko: 그 신문의 1면 제목은 산업에 혁명을 일으킬 수 있는 새로운 재생 에너지원의 발견을 발표했다.
quiz.hint: 신문 기사의 맨 위에 있는 큰 제목

quiz.sentence: The network sent its senior ___ to cover the international summit and provide live updates throughout the day.
quiz.sentence_ko: 그 네트워크는 국제 정상회담을 취재하고 하루 종일 실시간 업데이트를 제공하기 위해 자신의 선임 기자를 보냈다.

quiz.sentence: After the merger, the company plans to ___ all its warehouses in three major cities to reduce operating costs.
quiz.sentence_ko: 합병 후, 그 회사는 운영 비용을 줄이기 위해 모든 창고를 세 개의 주요 도시로 통합할 계획이다.

quiz.question: Your editor says 'We need more coverage of this story. The readers want to know every angle.' What does she want you to do?
options: Write fewer articles about the topic
Research and report the story from multiple perspectives and in greater detail
Ignore the story completely
Publish only one short article
quiz.explanation: Asking for more coverage means requesting more detailed and comprehensive reporting from different angles and viewpoints.
option_explanations: More coverage requires more articles, not fewer
Correct - more coverage means broader and deeper reporting from multiple angles
More coverage requires engagement with the story
More coverage requires substantial reporting, not just one short piece

quiz.question: Your manager says 'I'm delegating the event planning to you and your team. I trust you to make the decisions.' What responsibility have you just received?
options: You must report to the manager every hour about progress
You and your team are now responsible for organizing the event and making decisions about it
You must do all the work by yourself without any team help
The manager will still make all the important decisions about the event
quiz.explanation: When someone delegates a task, they give you the authority and responsibility to handle it, trusting your judgment and decision-making.
option_explanations: Delegation includes trust and autonomy, not constant micromanagement
Correct - delegation means you and your team are responsible for the task
Delegation distributes work to the team, not concentrates it
Delegation means you have decision-making authority

sentences.sentence: The breaking news headline was shared across social media within minutes of the announcement.
sentences.sentence_ko: 그 속보 헤드라인은 발표 후 몇 분 안에 소셜 미디어에서 공유되었다.
sentences.everyday_usage: 뉴스 기사의 제목을 지칭할 때 자주 사용됨

sentences.sentence: The war correspondent risked her life to report the truth from the conflict zone.
sentences.sentence_ko: 그 전쟁 특파원은 분쟁 지역에서 진실을 보도하기 위해 자신의 생명을 위험에 빠뜨렸다.
sentences.everyday_usage: 특정 지역을 담당하는 기자를 나타낼 때 사용

sentences.sentence: The Olympic Games received 24/7 coverage from broadcasters around the world.
sentences.sentence_ko: 올림픽 게임은 전 세계 방송사로부터 24시간 지속적인 보도를 받았다.
sentences.everyday_usage: 미디어가 사건을 보도하는 정도를 설명할 때

sentences.sentence: The startup decided to consolidate its product line and focus on three core offerings instead of ten.
sentences.sentence_ko: 그 스타트업은 자신의 제품군을 통합하고 10개 대신 3개의 핵심 제품에 집중하기로 결정했다.
sentences.everyday_usage: 여러 항목을 간소화하거나 통합할 때 사용

sentences.sentence: A good leader knows how to delegate tasks effectively without losing sight of the overall project goals.
sentences.sentence_ko: 좋은 리더는 전체 프로젝트 목표를 잃지 않으면서 효과적으로 업무를 위임하는 방법을 안다.
sentences.everyday_usage: 직장에서 업무를 다른 사람에게 맡길 때 사용
